paper.title: A Bayesian Approach for Stochastic Continuum-armed Bandit with Long-term Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic continuum-armed bandit with long-term constraints, noiseless constraint observations
unmapped: m unknown, possibly nonconvex constraint functions g_j observed exactly (noiselessly) after each action; long-term constraint (1/T) sum_t g(x_t) <= 0
Constraint violation V_T = ||[sum_t g(x_t)]_+|| is a second performance metric
RKHS assumption is on the penalised function F_l = f - sum_j kappa_j^l (psi(g_j)-1) with a possibly epoch-dependent kernel k_l, norm < B
extras 'safety_constraints' used as closest proxy for long-term (average) constraints
settings.definition_quote: the decision-maker chooses an action xt from a compact set X, and then observes a random reward value f^t(xt) and m constraint values {g_j^t(xt)}. ... f^t(xt) = f(xt) + εt ... In the first case, g_j^t(xt) = gj(xt), ∀j is deterministic. ... Our target is to maximize our expected reward f(x) with long-term constraints satisfied in expectation

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic continuum-armed bandit with long-term constraints, noisy constraint observations
unmapped: m unknown, possibly nonconvex constraint functions g_j observed with independent R-subGaussian noise; long-term constraint (1/T) sum_t g(x_t) <= 0
Constraint violation V_T = ||[sum_t g(x_t)]_+|| is a second performance metric
RKHS assumption is on G_l = f - sum_j kappa_j^l g_j with a possibly epoch-dependent kernel k_l, norm < B
extras 'safety_constraints' used as closest proxy for long-term (average) constraints

bound.regime: whenever the regret on the penalised objective is o(T)

conditions: algorithm applies an unconstrained bandit optimisation algorithm with sublinear regret to f - sum_j kappa_j Lambda(g_j) with fixed multipliers kappa_j and fixed penalty Lambda
there exist f, g in the setup for which regret and CV cannot both be sublinear

source.quote: For any fixed choices of κj and Λ(·) in (8), and any unconstrained bandit optimization algorithm M that can produce a sublinear regret for its objective function, applying M to (8) will fail to yield a sublinear regret and a sublinear CV for all forms of f (x) and g(x) in our setup.

results.notes: Impossibility statement for fixed-penalty approaches; proof constructs an instance where if the penalised regret is o(T) then CV >= cT/2 - o(T). Probability type not stated precisely; recorded loosely. Only for this restricted algorithm class.
